title: Quest board full-screen toggle
description: Operator instruction 2026-10-02, relayed via opum-doc seq 164 (opum-agent OPAG-1089): "add full screen mode and a toggle for it for the lore and quest mode". Design is opum-docs: docs/reference/pane-full-screen-and-quest-migration-skill-design.md at opum-ai/opum-doc main 945d0ae2, section 1. quest-cli builds the Quest board half; lore-cli builds the Lore pane half. Lands on dev with a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased, then rides into the 0.13.0 bump on #486.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Pressing z inside the Quest board pane and running /quest-board full each toggle between the normal size and the largest pane the surface allows, and the chosen state is stored with the pane prefs and restored at the next session
Full mode reopens the pane with focus and closeOnEscape left off, asking columns = viewport width minus a transcript margin when docked and rows = viewport height minus the prompt area when inline
The board draws list and detail side by side at 120 or more body columns and keeps its stacked layout below that threshold
The c collapse rail remains a third state reachable from full mode, and collapsing from full mode lands on the rail
When the surface keeps a size the person dragged or keyed instead of granting the request, the pane shows the one-line hint naming z rather than claiming the size it did not get

Each test the design names -- the toggle reopens with the expected columns and rows, the side-by-side layout draws at 120 or more body columns and stacked below, and the setting survives a reload -- runs on both the terminal and desktop surfaces

plan: 1. Read the board module: atoms, openPane, setCollapsed, prefs persistence, key handling, and the render layout
2. Add a full/normal state to the stored view, the z key and /quest-board full argument, and the reopen args per placement
3. Add the 120-body-column side-by-side layout with the collapse rail kept as a third state
4. Add the one-line hint for a size the surface did not grant
5. Extend tests/board.test.tsx across terminal and desktop surfaces
6. CHANGELOG under Unreleased, run bun run check, open the PR
implementationNotes:
QCLI-435 BUILT, 2026-10-02, session restored from QCLI-434. Design read by ref: opum-doc main 945d0ae2, docs/reference/pane-full-screen-and-quest-migration-skill-design.md section 1. All six acceptance criteria met; the quest-cli half only, the Lore pane's toggle is lore-cli's.

WHAT LANDED. hooks/quest.ts carries the pane geometry as pure functions -- fullPaneSize, paneSize, isWideLayout, isSizeHeld, fullAxis, sizeHeldHint -- so every size is computed and tested without a surface, and isStoredView moved here from register.tsx so the prefs reader is testable beside the writer. hooks/register.tsx adds isFull to the view and its saved prefs, the z hotkey and /quest-board full, the side-by-side layout at 120 body columns, and the held-size hint. tests/board.test.tsx gains 7 tests; the repository's full suite is 21 pass / 0 fail under the pinned bun 1.4.2.

THREE THINGS THE DESIGN LEFT OPEN, EACH DECIDED HERE AND WORTH A LOOK.

1. WHERE THE VIEWPORT COMES FROM, and this is the one that shaped the code. The design says full mode asks for "the viewport width minus a small transcript margin" but does not say how a pane learns the viewport. A draw is the only place both axes are known: ui.render carries e.viewport, command.run carries only presentation.columns, and session.start carries nothing at all -- measured in the engine's own declaration, not assumed. So a stored full mode opened at session.start cannot be sized, and the pane opens at the surface's default and asks again on the first draw, once per size (keyed on the requested size, so it is not a re-open on every draw). Building this any other way would have meant guessing a width at session.start.

2. THE PROMPT AREA HAS NO NUMBER IN THE DESIGN OR THE ENGINE. Inline full mode is "viewport height minus the prompt area"; nothing declares what that is. FULL_MARGIN_ROWS = 6, beside FULL_MARGIN_COLUMNS = 20 which the design does give. Flagged for opum-agent rather than settled silently.

3. THE GRANTED SIZE IS MEASURED INSIDE THE FRAME. Pane props say bodyColumns is "cells across the body, inside the frame", so a fully granted request still reads a few cells under what was asked, and comparing them directly would call every draw a held one. SIZE_SLACK = 4 absorbs the frame; a person's drag is larger than that.

A FOURTH, NOT OPEN BUT EASY TO GET WRONG: both axes are asked for in one $.ui.open rather than picking one from the placement. The engine ignores rows on the dock and columns inline, so asking both is right whichever shape the surface seats the pane in, and no guessing is needed before the pane is placed.

TESTS, AND THE PROOF THEY REJECT. Seven new: the size full mode asks for (including the rail winning over full, and one axis alone), the 120-column threshold, the held-size hint in both placements, the stored view surviving a reload, the z hotkey reopening with the expected columns and rows AND writing the choice back, the side-by-side layout, and the hint actually drawing. Every one that asserts a boundary was mutation-tested rather than only observed green: WIDE_COLUMNS 120 -> 100 reddens 2, FULL_MARGIN_COLUMNS 20 -> 10 reddens 3, SIZE_SLACK 4 -> 40 reddens 1, and making the hint never draw reddens the 2 that cover it. Each mutation reddens a PREDICTED SUBSET and leaves the rest green.

TYPECHECK CAVEAT. scripts/mod-test.mjs reports NOT TYPECHECKED -- no declaration for the running Claude Code 2.1.288 on this machine, and it deliberately does not fall back to another version's. So the module was typechecked here against the 2.1.287 declaration instead, which is a different measurement and is named as one: tsc exit 0, with a negative control (a bogus property on fullPaneSize's return) confirming the declaration actually resolved rather than the check passing vacuously. That is pre-existing on this machine, not introduced by this change.

DEPENDENCIES UNCHANGED: no binary source, no package version, no lockfile. The six platform packages committed on #486 are untouched by this work.
finalSummary:
Full-screen mode for the Quest board, from the operator's instruction via opum-doc seq 164: z and /quest-board full toggle between the largest pane the surface allows and the normal size, the choice is stored with the pane's prefs and restored next session, the list and detail draw side by side from 120 body columns, c still collapses to the rail as a third state, and a size the surface kept rather than granted is said on one line rather than claimed.

Landed on dev by squash merge as opum-ai/quest-cli#489 at baa10e37, with all three required contexts (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check) a completed success on that PR head. Verification: bun run check exit 0 under the pinned bun 1.4.2 -- repository suite and mod suite, 21 pass / 0 fail on the mod side. Seven new tests in tests/board.test.tsx, each running on both the terminal and desktop surfaces. Mutation-tested rather than only observed green: WIDE_COLUMNS 120->100 reddens 2, FULL_MARGIN_COLUMNS 20->10 reddens 3, SIZE_SLACK 4->40 reddens 1, and making the hint never draw reddens the 2 that cover it.

Three choices the design left open were decided in code and reported to opum-agent rather than settled quietly; all three were accepted and are now written into the design (opum-doc seq 167). How a pane opened before any draw learns the viewport -- ui.render is the only place both axes are known, so a stored full mode opens at the surface default and asks again on the first draw. FULL_MARGIN_ROWS = 6, since neither the design nor the engine gives a number for the prompt area. SIZE_SLACK = 4, because bodyColumns is measured inside the frame and a fully granted request otherwise reads as a drag.

Typecheck caveat, named rather than implied: scripts/mod-test.mjs reports NOT TYPECHECKED on this machine for the running Claude Code 2.1.288, and deliberately does not fall back to another version's declaration. The module was typechecked against the 2.1.287 declaration with a negative control confirming it resolved.
